item.title: Higher-Order Functions Are Not Free: The reduce That's Secretly O(n²)
item.description: There is a piece of advice that gets repeated until it sounds like a law: prefer map, filter, and reduce over a for loop, because they are more efficient. The first half is reasonable. The second half is wrong, and believing it has cost us real frame time. Higher-order functions are a readability tool, not a speed tool, and at least one of them has a default that turns an innocent one-liner into O(n²).
